questions.prompt: You have built and tested an application locally. The publish directory contains all ready-to-run files, including the entry point. ZIP deployment will use its default extraction path with build automation disabled. Which archive layout should you deploy?

options.text: Place the contents of the publish directory directly at the ZIP root.
options.explanation: ZIP deployment extracts into the app content directory. Putting the published contents at the archive root preserves the expected entry-point layout.

options.text: Place the publish directory itself at the ZIP root with the files nested inside it.
options.explanation: Including the enclosing publish directory adds a level below the app content root instead of placing the entry point at its expected location.

options.text: Place the published files inside a wwwroot directory at the ZIP root.
options.explanation: The default deployment destination is already wwwroot. This extra directory nests the application one level too deep.

options.text: Place the unbuilt source directory contents directly at the ZIP root.
options.explanation: Build automation is disabled. The archive needs the tested ready-to-run output rather than source that still requires build tasks.

questions.prompt: What happens when an administrator changes App Service app settings?

options.text: The updated settings are passed as environment variables after an app restart.
options.explanation: App Service injects app settings into the runtime environment and triggers an app restart when settings are added, removed, or edited.

options.text: The updated settings become environment variables without restarting the running app.
options.explanation: A settings edit triggers a restart; it is not merely an in-place change to the running process environment.

options.text: The updated settings are written into source configuration files before a rebuild.
options.explanation: App settings are runtime environment configuration. Saving them does not require rewriting source files and rebuilding the application.

options.text: The updated settings remain pending until the next application package deployment.
options.explanation: Saving an app-settings change triggers the restart that applies it; a separate package deployment is not required.

questions.prompt: An App Service app reads blobs using a token for its system-assigned managed identity. Token acquisition and network access succeed, but blob reads fail authorization. The identity has no blob data role, and no deny assignments or role conditions apply. Which role assignment authorizes this app to read the blobs?

options.text: Assign Storage Blob Data Reader to the app identity at the target container.
options.explanation: The app uses its managed identity for blob data requests. This role grants that principal read access to blobs in the target container.

options.text: Assign Reader to the app identity at the storage account.
options.explanation: Reader grants management-plane visibility, not the blob data permissions needed for token-authenticated reads.

options.text: Assign Website Contributor to the app identity at the web app.
options.explanation: Permission to manage the web app does not grant its identity read access to the target container data.

options.text: Assign Storage Blob Data Reader to the deployment user at the target container.
options.explanation: The request token represents the app identity, not the deployment user. Granting the user access does not authorize the app principal.
